definitions.explanation: The feeling of being moved or impressed by something excellent or praiseworthy.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{感心|かんしん}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I was impressed by his effort.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{若|わか}い→若い：00823_wakai⟧⟦のに→のに：10529_noni⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{礼儀|れいぎ}{正|ただ}しくて→礼儀正しい：15088_reigitadashii⟧、⟦{皆|みな}→皆：01810_mina⟧{感心|かんしん}⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: She was so polite despite being young that everyone was impressed.

notes:
{感心|かんしん} expresses admiration or being impressed. It can function as a noun, suru-verb, or na-adjective.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive)
- No standard transitive pair
- Pattern: {感心|かんしん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {感心|かんしん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be impressed)
- {感心|かんしん}な〜 (admirable ~)
- 〜⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{感心|かんしん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be impressed by ~)

USAGE:
- ⟦あまり→あまり：00604_amari⟧{感心|かんしん}⟦しない→する：00392_suru⟧/⟦できない→できる：00557_dekiru⟧: expresses disapproval or not being impressed
- This is an indirect way to criticize something

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {感心|かんしん} vs. ⟦{関心|かんしん}→関心：00182_kanshin⟧: Different kanji!
  - {感心|かんしん}: admiration (⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧ = feeling)
  - ⟦{関心|かんしん}→関心：00182_kanshin⟧: interest ({関|かん} = relation)

REGISTER: Neutral to slightly formal
